units.plan: x and y in metres in the capture's world frame, z up; room polygons counter-clockwise
units.scope_quantity: the unit named on each line item (SF, LF, EA, m2 or m)
units.score: detector score in [0, 1] after cross-view merge, not a calibrated probability

interval.method: lidar tier error model. Lengths: sigma = sqrt((v*s)^2 + a^2) with a scale term s = 0.003 shared by every measurement (the larger of the tier floor and the geometry's estimate, with the scale spread across video chunks or the scale error of a rejected loop closure) and additive terms a = 0.008 m (walls), 0.006 m (heights), 0.012 m (openings), 0.020 m (damage), inflated for thin evidence on the measurement and on a wall's two end walls (low observed fraction, few face points, fit residuals in quadrature, low light, fewer than 4 photos or views, missing focal length). A wall ending at a wall with no face of its own may run on by 0.15 of the room's extent along it (at most 3 times the wall's length) and is no shorter than the part of its face that was seen. A wall ending at an unobserved wall or a step (shorter than 0.50 m, or shorter than 1.00 m and low) may be a fragment: its upper bound reaches the pieces beyond the step or the room's extent along the wall. Heights add a vertical term of 0.00 (log); an unobserved floor or ceiling widens the upper side by z*0.50 m, an unobserved ceiling up to 4.0 m; a door with no head edge found reaches down to 1.90 m. Areas: sqrt((2*A*s)^2 + (sum of L_i*a_i)^2) plus unobserved wall positions, and upward to the bounding box when a wall may be a fragment. Footprint: scale term fully correlated across rooms plus independent per-room terms; unplaced rooms widen footprint and extents 1.5x. Interval = value - z*q*sigma to value + z*q*sigma_hi with z = 1.645, the one-sided terms widening only their side, lo clipped at 0; q = 1.00, prior value: not calibrated, this tier has fewer than 9 ground-truth rooms. Wall surface areas combine the length, height and opening intervals by interval arithmetic.

definitions.wall_length: face to face at 1 m height between the two neighbouring walls, along the room polygon edge
definitions.wall_height: floor plane to ceiling plane distance at the wall
definitions.ceiling_height: floor plane to ceiling plane distance inside the room
definitions.opening_width: clear width between the jamb faces
definitions.opening_height: floor to the underside of the head for doors and passages; inside the frame for windows
definitions.opening_offset: along the wall, from the wall start to the near jamb of the opening
definitions.floor_area: polygon area of the interior wall faces
definitions.perimeter: sum of the room's wall lengths
definitions.wall_surface_area: wall length times wall height minus the areas of the openings in that wall
definitions.ceiling_surface_area: equal to the floor area (flat ceiling assumed)
definitions.footprint: sum of the room floor areas; walls between rooms are not included
definitions.extent: size of the bounding box of all room polygons along plan x and plan y
definitions.damage_extent: width along the surface u axis and height along v of the damage region; area of its mask projected onto the surface; walls use u from the wall start and v from the floor, floors and ceilings use plan x and y

concealed_damage_flags.title: Crack from an opening corner, possible movement at the header
concealed_damage_flags.basis: Project heuristic, no standard cited: stress concentrates at the corners of door and window openings, so cracks that start there are a common sign of settlement or deflection of the header or lintel.
concealed_damage_flags.recommendation: Check whether the door or window sticks or racks and whether the crack is growing (mark its ends and date them). Have the framing over the opening inspected if it is.

concealed_damage_flags.title: Crack longer than 1 m, structural check
concealed_damage_flags.basis: Project heuristic, no standard cited: a crack over 1 m is long enough that foundation or framing movement is a plausible cause. Crack width, which matters more for structure, cannot be measured from the capture.
concealed_damage_flags.recommendation: Measure the crack width on site and have a structural engineer look at it if it is wider than a hairline, stepped, or tapered.
